outcome: Judged: the only event is Kawauchi's March 2023 claimed proof (arXiv:2303.04368), which predates the snapshot and is set aside as not credible, so the conjecture stays open. [Judged 2026-09-28; the researcher's original outcome follows.] Akio Kawauchi posted a preprint (arXiv:2303.04368, v1 March 2023, v2 revised April 2024) claiming a complete proof of the Whitehead aspherical conjecture via ribbon sphere-link methods, and published it in a low-quality open-access venue (Journal of Mathematical Techniques and Computational Mathematics, 3(5), 2024); it has not been digested, endorsed, or cited by the topology community, and the conjecture's own Wikipedia article and other surveys still treat it as open as of the window.

disputes.summary: Kawauchi's arXiv preprint claims a full, affirmative proof of the Whitehead conjecture, but it has not been independently verified, cited, or endorsed by topologists. It was published in the Journal of Mathematical Techniques and Computational Mathematics (Opast Publishers), which shows multiple hallmarks of a low-quality/predatory open-access venue (extremely broad and unfocused subject scope spanning topics like 'Vedic Mathematics' and 'Collaborative Robots', a small and under-verified editorial board, an unverifiable claimed impact factor, and an unfinished website). No expert digestion, review, or citation of the claimed proof by other topologists was found.

summary: The triage correctly identified Akio Kawauchi's arXiv preprint 2303.04368 ('Whitehead aspherical conjecture via ribbon sphere-link') as the only substantive lead. Its v1 was posted March 2023 (before the window) but v2 was revised 9 April 2024 (inside the window), and it was subsequently published in 2024 in the Journal of Mathematical Techniques and Computational Mathematics, a venue that on inspection shows several red flags of a low-quality/predatory open-access publisher (implausibly broad scope, thin and unverifiable editorial credentials, an unverified impact factor claim, and an incomplete website). I found no evidence that any topologist has reviewed, endorsed, cited, or engaged with the claimed proof — no MathOverflow thread, no blog digestion (Tao, n-category cafe, etc.), no citation in a subsequent paper treating it as settled. Kawauchi has continued to publish supporting lemmas ('Free ribbon lemma for surface-link', arXiv:2412.09281, Dec 2024, and 'Another proof of free ribbon lemma', arXiv:2408.04793) that build on his own apparatus, but these are self-referential extensions, not independent corroboration. The conjecture's Wikipedia article, as fetched live, still presents it as unresolved with no mention of Kawauchi's claim. I also found and set aside two things that are out of scope for this exact bullet: (1) A. M. Mikhovich's 2025 Izvestiya Mathematics paper on rational and p-adic analogues of Whitehead's conjecture — this changes the hypotheses (working over prounipotent/pro-p settings) rather than restricting the stated integral conjecture, so it is a related problem, not a case, per §3.1. (2) A February 2026 GitHub issue in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures cataloguing the Whitehead asphericity conjecture as a Lean formalization target — this is explicitly AI-agent-generated (per the issue text, 'generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me') but it is only a formalization-difficulty assessment (rated 4/5 difficulty, noting missing Mathlib infrastructure) with no proof, no formalized statement, and no PR — it documents that the conjecture exists and is hard to formalize, which is not itself a mathematical event about the problem. I also found a long, numbered, AI-flavored WordPress post (ppalme.wordpress.com, 8 Sept 2026) that explicitly disclaims proving the conjecture and instead offers a speculative 'reformulation framework'; it names no AI tool and does not meet the bar for any ai_role above none, and in any case asserts no result. No counterexample, no disproof, and no accepted proof of the actual Whitehead conjecture as stated was found anywhere in the window. I classify status as 'claimed' rather than 'open' because a specific, complete proof claim by a named mathematician exists and was revised/republished within the window, but 'resolved' is wrong because no expert digestion exists and the publication venue does not confer real peer review credibility. No AI system was found to be involved in any of the substantive mathematical work (Kawauchi's papers show no AI attribution at all); the only AI-agent-authored artifact found (the DeepMind GitHub issue) did not produce any mathematics, only a formalization-scoping note, so ai_role is 'none' for the record as a whole.
competing_reading: One could argue the Kawauchi preprint should be scored 'open' rather than 'claimed', treating an unreviewed, predatory-adjacent-journal publication as equivalent to no claim at all. I chose 'claimed' because the rubric's bar for 'claimed' is just 'a preprint, announcement or machine-checked certificate that experts have not yet digested' — Kawauchi's arXiv posting satisfies that literally, and the 2024 revision date falls inside the window, so treating it as a non-event would understate what actually happened (a serious, specific, dated proof claim was made and is now circulating, however uncorroborated).
what_would_settle_it: A citation or public statement by a recognized topologist engaging with Kawauchi's ribbon sphere-link argument (accepting, refuting, or identifying a specific gap), or a retraction/erratum from Kawauchi himself, or acceptance in a mainstream topology journal.
